authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses a lossless CST against TWO grammars, chosen by file suffix: KerML and SysML have two start symbols, and sv2_syntax::parse requires a Language with no default (ADR-0014). It reads packages, imports, aliases, annotating elements as members, KerML's eight classifiers and its Feature in both forms, SysML's eight definitions plus PortDefinition, seven usages with all five feature specializations, and both keywordless usages. It reads the DECLARATION LAYER of requirements, constraints, calculations and actions: RequirementDefinition, ConstraintDefinition, CalculationDefinition, ActionDefinition and their three specialised bodies (RequirementBody, CalculationBody, ActionBody), SubjectMember, RequirementConstraintMember, ReturnParameterMember, ActionUsage and PerformActionUsage. The expression layer reads the fifteen precedence tiers, the postfix pair FeatureChainExpression and BracketExpression, and now the INVOCATION -- InvocationExpression over ArgumentList in both its positional and named forms -- and the reference layer reads OwnedFeatureChain. 166 of 558 productions. Diagnostics are typed: Parse::errors() returns Diagnostic, each with a TextRange, a namespaced code and a severity, and OffsetMap is the single designated offset boundary. The reference grammar is DERIVED IN FULL and FROZEN at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b: 554 of 554 live units verified in both languages. The RUST parser accepts 46 of 253 .sysml and 17 of 58 .kerml corpus files, recorded per file in tests/corpus-accepted.txt and ratcheted by scripts/corpus_sweep.py: the set may grow and must never shrink.
authored.next_step:
IMPLEMENT InitialNodeMember, the smallest piece of the CONTROL-FLOW LAYER, which is all that is left of ActionBodyItem and is now the largest unimplemented cluster in the corpus by a wide margin.

    InitialNodeMember = MemberPrefix 'first' memberFeature = [QualifiedName]
                        RelationshipBody                      (SysML 8.2.2.17.1)

Every part of that body is already implemented -- member_prefix, qualified_name and relationship_body all exist -- so this is ONE TABLE ROW of work. Write `initial_node_member` in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs beside `return_parameter_member`, add the node kind to NODES in scripts/gen_syntax_kinds.py, and dispatch it in `body_elements` beside the `admits_return_parameter` arm. It needs a new `Body` predicate: ActionBodyItem is reached by ActionBody (8.2.2.17.1) AND by CalculationBodyItem (8.2.2.19), so the predicate is true for Body::Action and Body::Calculation -- work out from the clauses whether Body::Requirement and Body::Definition reach it too before widening it to them, because that is exactly the mistake tests/rejection/return-parameter-member-is-not-an-action-body-item.sysml was written to catch in the other direction.

THEN the rest of the alternation, in this order and for this reason:

    ActionBodyItem = NonBehaviorBodyItem                       <- implemented
                   | InitialNodeMember ActionTargetSuccessionMember*
                   | SourceSuccessionMember? ActionBehaviorMember
                     ActionTargetSuccessionMember*
                   | GuardedSuccessionMember                   (SysML 8.2.2.17.1)

`first` is the cheap half and `then` is the expensive one. SourceSuccessionMember is `'then' SourceSuccession` (8.2.2.9.3) and ActionTargetSuccessionMember reaches TargetSuccession = `SourceEndMember 'then' ConnectorEndMember` (8.2.2.17.8), so `then` needs the CONNECTOR END machinery -- ConnectorEndMember and SourceEndMember -- which nothing implements yet. Do not start at `then` because it leads the histogram.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken after the invocation landed, over the 248 corpus files the parser still rejects. This is a count of files that WRITE each construct, not a first-error histogram, because lesson (1) below says the latter says where to start and not what a change will buy:

    then         59 files / 301 occurrences   control flow, needs connector ends
    end          46 / 258                     EndUsagePrefix, unimplemented in SysML
    flow         38 / 110                     FlowUsage
    first        31 / 121                     control flow, InitialNodeMember
    assert       28 /  53                     AssertConstraintUsage

    state        22 / 169                     StateDefinition, needs StateBody
    metadata     21 /  62     accept 21 / 91  interface 19 / 74   if 19 / 26
    objective    18 /  30     succession 17 / 56

Regenerate this with the scratch script pattern: read tests/corpus-accepted.txt (paths contain SPACES, so split on lines and not on whitespace -- that bug made the first run of this measurement report all 311 files as failing), subtract it from vendor/corpus, and histogram the leading keyword of every line.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

RESOLVED: the derive-grammar six-phase pipeline. It runs, and the expression layer is being derived through it starting from KerML 8.2.5.8.1. Two pipeline defects had to be fixed first (plan enumerated the Xtext inventory; freeze check went red on the first derived unit); both are fixed and tested.

RESOLVED: positional, and the position cannot be reached from both sides. A '[' reached from UsageDeclaration's FeatureSpecializationPart is a MultiplicityRange (SysML 8.2.2.6.6); a '[' reached after a primary expression operand is a BracketExpression (KerML 8.2.5.8.2). The hypothesis held for every corpus shape. The decisive line is `attribute mass : MassValue[1] = 1200 [kg];`, which writes BOTH roles and parses: multiplicity_part is reachable only from feature_specialization_part, which sits inside UsageDeclaration, and a UsageDeclaration is finished before the ValuePart's '=' is read, so the two can never contend for one token. What separates the productions themselves is the OPERAND: a BracketExpression has one before the '[' and a MultiplicityRange has none, which is what tests/rejection/bracket-expression-needs-an-operand.sysml holds. The corpus also writes a bracketed name (`[one]`, `[spatialCF]`, `[source]`) that is indistinguishable from a multiplicity bound by CONTENT, which is why content was never a candidate rule. Both roles are implemented and 297 corpus files are no longer blocked on this; acceptance went 32 to 39 .sysml when BracketExpression landed.

Is MAX_DEPTH = 400 in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs the right recursion limit, and should it be configurable? It was introduced because the recursive expression parser OVERFLOWED THE STACK, which aborts the process and so is strictly worse than the panic invariant 3 forbids. Measured thresholds before the guard: unary operators between 2000 and 5000 levels, parenthesised expressions and nested bodies between 5000 and 10000. 400 is far past anything a person writes, but it is a number nobody derived from a source, and it changes what the parser accepts.

WIDENED by the postfix expressions. DEPTH IS A PROPERTY OF THE TREE, NOT OF THE PARSER'S RECURSION, and the feature chain proved it: `postfix_tail` is a LOOP and uses no stack at all, yet a 50000-link chain aborted a test thread, because every link wraps the last and the tree is as deep as the chain is long. Folding also stopped being linear at that size. Chains and brackets are therefore counted against the same budget as nested bodies. Anything else that folds -- IndexExpression, FunctionOperationExpression, CollectExpression, SelectExpression, all of which join the same loop -- must count too, and the loop is the place to enforce it once.

pending_decisions.question:
A rejection file can go stale without the sweep noticing, and this session produced one. tests/rejection/action-usage-is-not-an-action-definition.sysml held `action brake;` and `perform action stop;`. When ActionUsage landed the first line began to parse; the file went on being rejected because of the second, so the sweep stayed green while the file's header comment described a rule the parser no longer had. It was found by reading, not by a check. corpus_sweep.py asserts only that each file is rejected, never WHY, so every multi-construct rejection file is a place this can happen again, and the set is 97 files and growing by three or four per production. Candidate fix: have each rejection file name the diagnostic it expects -- a code, or a line number, or the first error's text -- and have the sweep check that the rejection is the one the comment claims. Cheapest honest version is probably a header directive like `// expect: PARSE-UNEXPECTED at 3:2` parsed by corpus_sweep.py, which also makes the by-rule versus by-absence distinction machine-readable for the first time. Not attempted: it is a change to the harness rather than the parser, and planting a failure to prove the new check bites is most of the work.

A SECOND INSTANCE of the same class, found by the reviewer at session close and not in a rejection file at all: three code comments cited KerML 8.2.2.6 to establish that `ref`, `action` and `constraint` are reserved and therefore not names. KerML 8.2.2.6 lists KerML's OWN reserved words and contains none of the three; SysML 8.2.2.1.2 is the clause that reserves them. The disambiguation was correct and the citation was not, which invariant 4 counts as the expensive kind of wrong because it reads as evidence. Nothing in the gate compares a cited clause against what the comment claims of it, and check_citations.py only verifies that a named receipt was pinned. Worth considering alongside this decision: the two are the same failure -- a claim that still passes after the thing it claimed stopped being true.
blocks: trusting the rejection corpus to mean what its comments say as it grows

pending_decisions.question:
Is there another production marked `// production: X` whose function does not read all of X's body? This decision was opened when four reference productions were found marked while the OwnedFeatureChain alternative of SysML 8.2.2.6.5 was absent, and a reviewer then found a fifth of the same shape (OwnedFeatureTyping). All five are fixed and share one `chainable_target`. The alternation that had five instances is now exhaustively checked; NO OTHER SHAPE IS, so the question stands for the rest of the grammar.

APPLIED PROSPECTIVELY FOR THE FIRST TIME this session, which is the cheapest form of the fix and needs no gate check: InstantiatedTypeMember (KerML 8.2.5.8.3) is `InstantiatedTypeReference | OwnedFeatureChainMember`, the invocation reads only the first alternative, and it was left UNMARKED while the eight productions around it were marked. The node is built; the alternation is not claimed. Doing that at the time costs nothing, and it is what the four-then-five defects cost when it was not done.

A false `implemented` is still the one coverage error that cannot be found by reading the report, because the report is what is wrong. bnf_coverage.py counts markers; it cannot compare a function against the rule body it claims. Candidate check, unchanged: for each marked production, assert that every literal keyword in its derived rule appears in the marked function and that every `alt` arm is reachable. Weak, but it would have caught all five.
blocks: trusting the coverage percentage as a measure of what parses

pending_decisions.question:
Nothing in the gate compares a CITED CLAUSE against what the comment claims of it, and this session produced SIX instances across three review passes -- enough to call it the repository's characteristic defect rather than a run of bad luck. They split into two kinds.

WRONG CLAUSE NUMBER, or a right number carrying a false argument:
  (1) three comments cited KerML 8.2.2.6 for `ref`, `action` and `constraint` being reserved; that clause lists KerML's OWN reserved words and contains none of the three. SysML 8.2.2.1.2 is the clause that reserves them.
  (2) `calculation_definition` said CalculationDefinition is NOT an OccurrenceDefinition 'unlike the sibling it shares a body with'. It IS one, via ActionDefinition > Behavior, where ConstraintDefinition reaches it via Predicate. The CONCLUSION was right and the ARGUMENT was false, which is the shape nobody rereads.
  (3) and (4) `definition_element` and `usage_element` cited SysML 8.2.2.6.1 for the DefinitionElement/UsageElement alternation; both are stated at 8.2.2.5.2, and 8.2.2.6.1 merely USES DefinitionElement inside DefinitionMember.

MISQUOTED METACLASS under a correct clause number -- a new sub-kind, found in the invocation commit and the cheapest of all to check mechanically:
  (5) `InstantiatedTypeReference : Feature` where the clause and the pinned inventory both say `Type`.
  (6) `NamedArgumentMember : ParameterMembership` where both say `FeatureMembership`. That one also hid a real fact: a named argument's membership is NOT the ParameterMembership its positional sibling ArgumentMember is, and the wrong transcription erased the distinction it should have drawn.

All six are fixed. Every one passed the gate.

THE SUB-KIND IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE TODAY and the check is small: every marked production's comment writes `Name : Metaclass = body`, and .claude/state/grammar/bnf-productions.json carries `metaclass` for each rule. Comparing the two is a string equality over the productions already marked -- it needs no wiki, so it runs on a fresh clone, which is the standing limit that blocks the harder version. That would have caught (5) and (6) and nothing else. The wider check -- retrieve each cited clause and assert the production names in the comment appear in it -- would have caught (1), (3) and (4), and needs the wikis. (2) is a claim about a specialization chain and would need index/specialization-tree.json.

check_citations.py only verifies that a named receipt was pinned; it never opens the clause. Same family as [rejection-provenance] and [coverage-marker-audit]: a claim that still passes after the thing it claimed stopped being true. Of the three, THIS one now has the cheapest first increment, and that increment is the recommended next move on all three.
blocks: trusting any clause citation in the codebase without re-retrieving it

log.summary: Closed the SysML grammar and froze the reference. 473 to 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict; frozen at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b, 554 productions, ledger entry 1. The oracle went from 155 to all 311 corpus files accepted, still catching all 37 negatives with none leaked. Four filed specification defects repaired and recorded, each issue page fetched and read: SYSML21-408 and -624 (both in SendNode's single line), -400 (ControlNodePrefix) and -401 (TriggerExpression). ForVariableDeclarationMember adjudicated, which left SysML with no unreachable production. The oracle's state guard was re-derived from a measurement: ~143 items per token scaling linearly, so the 400_000 absolute cap was mis-calibrated rather than the grammar ambiguous, and it is now a per-token budget with four tests. Also declared sv2-ast, sv2-hir and sv2-resolve as stub crates, and proposed ADR-0016 and ADR-0017.

Implemented the expression operator core: OwnedExpression by precedence climbing over the fifteen tiers of KerML 8.2.5.8.1 table 6, plus MultiplicityPart, ValuePart and ElementFilterMember, which it unblocked. Coverage 57 to 106 of 558; negative cases 49 to 65. Precedence is NOT in the grammar and cannot be -- note 2 of that clause says so -- so the parser reads docs/operator-precedence.toml, and a test diffs that file against the parser's INFIX table both ways so neither can be edited alone; deviations.json had already recorded the decision under BinaryOperatorExpression as spec_only/follow_spec. Found and fixed a defect this introduced: deep nesting overflowed the stack, which aborts rather than panics and so breaks invariant 3; added MAX_DEPTH and a round-trip test at 50000 levels for parentheses, unary operators and nested bodies. spec-conformance-reviewer returned one blocking finding, all fixed: the FeatureSpecializationPart comment quoted the Pilot's '( -> FeatureSpecialization )+' syntactic predicate as though it were KerML 8.2.4.3.1, and that '->' is in neither specification's BNF. Also committed a draft docs/CRATES.md and the author's spelling corrections to README.md and NOTICE.md.

Ten commits closing the requirement, constraint and action DECLARATION layers. Coverage 133 to 156 of 558; acceptance 29 to 44 .sysml; rejection corpus 77 to 97 files. Added RequirementDefinition and RequirementBody, SubjectMember, ConstraintDefinition with CalculationBody and ResultExpressionMember, RequirementConstraintMember, ActionDefinition with ActionBody, ActionUsage and PerformActionUsage; in the expression layer FeatureChainExpression and BracketExpression, which share one left-folding postfix loop; in the reference layer OwnedFeatureChain. RESOLVED [bracket-role]: the two roles of '[' are told apart by POSITION and cannot contend, because multiplicity_part is reachable only from feature_specialization_part, which is finished before the ValuePart's '=' is read; `attribute mass : MassValue[1] = 1200 [kg];` writes both and parses. FOUND AND FIXED A COVERAGE OVERCLAIM: four reference productions were marked while the OwnedFeatureChain alternative was absent; new pending decision [coverage-marker-audit] asks whether others are. MADE AN ADJUDICATION TESTABLE: the RequirementConstraintUsage conflict, resolved follow_spec in September, could not be checked until both bodies existed, and `require someRef { a <= b }` is now the rejection file that fails if the parser ever drifts to the Pilot's reading. Two defects caught by their own tests: a 50000-link feature chain aborted a test thread although the fold is a loop, because the TREE is as deep as the chain is long, and chains are now bounded by MAX_DEPTH like any nesting; and a test asserting `subject;` was rejected was wrong, because Identification is fully optional and an anonymous subject is grammatical. New pending decision [rejection-provenance] records a rejection file that went stale silently. The action layer's reading is CORRECTED: it was a 37-file lever meaning declarations, not successions -- control flow led one failing file before this work and nine after it.

Four commits closing the calculation layer and opening the invocation. Coverage 156 to 166 of 558; acceptance 44 to 46 .sysml and 15 to 17 .kerml, the first KerML movement since the language split; rejection corpus 97 to 103. Added CalculationDefinition, ReturnParameterMember, and the invocation family -- InvocationExpression, InstantiatedTypeReference, ArgumentList, PositionalArgumentList, NamedArgumentList, NamedArgumentMember, NamedArgument and ParameterRedefinition. LESSON (1) EARNED A FOURTH AND FIFTH TIME, and this time it was applied BEFORE the work rather than after: state.json predicted CalculationDefinition would buy three corpus files, and it bought ZERO, because all thirteen files that write `calc def` also write `return` -- measured before the code was written, and the rejection file being deleted said so in its own comment. ReturnParameterMember then bought one, not thirteen, because twelve of those files have a further blocker. The invocation bought three, two of them KerML, all three the same MassRollup model written twice. A TEST EXPECTATION WAS WRONG AND THE PARSER WAS RIGHT: `f(a, b)` builds THREE EmptyResultMembers because KerML 8.2.5.8.3 names one in FeatureReferenceExpression as well, and each argument is one; the count was corrected to what the clause states and `f()` added to isolate the invocation's own, rather than the assertion being loosened. APPLIED [coverage-marker-audit] PROSPECTIVELY for the first time: InstantiatedTypeMember was left unmarked because only one of its two alternatives is read. The spec-conformance-reviewer ran twice and found FOUR FALSE CLAIMS, all fixed: CalculationDefinition wrongly said NOT to be an OccurrenceDefinition, 8.2.2.6.1 cited for an alternation stated at 8.2.2.5.2, and then two MISQUOTED METACLASSES under correct clause numbers -- `InstantiatedTypeReference : Feature` for `Type` and `NamedArgumentMember : ParameterMembership` for `FeatureMembership`. With the three from the previous session that is six instances, and the new pending decision [comment-claim-checking] records that the metaclass sub-kind is checkable today by string equality against bnf-productions.json, with no wiki and so on a fresh clone. The invocation commit's own message also had an off-by-one -- it said acceptance went 44 to 46 .sysml when its parent already stood at 45 -- corrected in the follow-up commit rather than amended away. OPERATIONAL DEFECT, mine, fully repaired: a `git add -A` swept a 3.0 GB untracked WebStorm install into the ReturnParameterMember commit. Nothing was pushed; the commit was rebuilt by soft reset as 8565c00 with the eleven real files, verified byte-identical on the non-WebStorm paths, and the orphaned objects were reflog-expired and collected, taking .git from 1.1 GB to 3.9 MB. No branch, tag or remote ever contained them and ui/shell was never involved. Staging in this repository is by explicit path from here on.
